focus.jtag: Monday the S&P 500 jumped 4.73% to 7,237.17 — its second-biggest point gain ever — after Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, sparking a broad AI-led rally; the Nasdaq surged 6.51% and the VIX plunged ~25% to 26.62. This morning futures are fading ~1% as traders test the rally, the VIX is back near 28–30, and a Dec 9 Fed hike is ~94% priced. The scanner boarded 3 fresh Type-A post-earnings gaps (A, AMTM, FRO).
focus.jnote: The whole story is a one-day melt-up already giving back ground, with the VIX still above 25 — and a scanner that boarded 3 fresh post-earnings gaps into that chop. On Monday the S&P 500 appreciated 4.7% or 326.78 points to finish at 7,237.17, with the Nasdaq up 6.51% and the Dow up 3.01%. A single CEO decision sent the market soaring after seven straight losing days — Nvidia shares jumped about 31% after the board reinstated Jensen Huang. The VIX dropped 24.63% to 27.05, and the fear gauge closed at 26.62, down ~9–25% depending on the source. But Tuesday is a give-back: Dow futures fell 0.5%, S&P 500 futures declined 1%, and Nasdaq-100 contracts fell 2% after stocks logged their best day since the 'Liberation Day' recovery of April 2025. Even after Monday, the index is out of correction territory but still well short of its high — about 7.4% below the record. A Sniper does not lean hard into a fading one-day melt-up with the VIX this stretched — the 3 boarded names are take-at-half-size-at-most, not table-pounders.
focus.notdown: The boarded bullish names are all Type A post-earnings gaps, not a sector theme. Agilent is the cleanest: Agilent topped fourth-quarter earnings and revenue estimates after the close Monday on higher lab-device demand, and shares are up ~6.8% premarket after a 3.3% regular-session gain. But the scanner itself flags reaction-day volume near zero — far below the 1.3× confirmation bar — so these are gap-holding, not volume-confirmed. In a fading melt-up with the VIX ~28–30, that's half-size at most on the A+, watch-only on the rest.
focus.notup: There is no clean 'Not-Up' name today. Selling bear calls into a tape that just logged its best day since April 2025 — and is now chopping two-sided on every AI headline — is its own squeeze trap. US stock futures fell on Tuesday, building on a blistering rally, as investors took stock of what's next for Nvidia and the AI trade now that Jensen Huang is back as CEO. With a Dec 9 Fed hike nearly priced and the melt-up still digesting, the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new on the bear side today.
focus.why: Why RED? Three things stack. One: composite 70 is HOT and P(≥1% gap) at ~44% is well above the 35% trigger — either alone locks out GREEN. Two: Monday's +4.73% was a one-day, headline-driven melt-up that is already fading ~1% pre-open, with the VIX back near 28–30 after closing at 26.62 — a stretched, two-sided tape. Three: a December 9 Fed hike is ~94% priced, a structural cap just two weeks out. The scanner did board 3 fresh Type-A gaps — but all on near-zero reaction volume. Take the A+ (Agilent) at half size only if it validates at 9:35; treat AMTM and FRO as watch-only. Keep any DTE clear of the Dec 9 FOMC. Cash is a position today.

setups.read: Cleanest name on the board. Agilent's Q4 EPS of $1.86 beat the $1.73 forecast by 7.5%, and revenue of $2.04B topped the $1.99B estimate — a clean double-beat, with quarterly sales topping $2 billion for the first time in its history. The stock is gapping well: shares are up ~6.8% premarket after a 3.3% regular-session gain Monday. Baird raised its target to $208 and maintained Outperform. The one real caveat is the scanner's own flag: reaction-day volume came in near 0.00×, far below the 1.3× confirmation bar, and there's only one S/R layer (the $176.04 gap floor, −6.7%). Next earnings ~Feb 22, well outside any DTE.

risks: A one-day melt-up already fading — S&P futures fell 1% and Nasdaq-100 contracts fell 2% Tuesday after stocks logged their best day since the April 2025 'Liberation Day' recovery. A give-back that retraces more of Monday's +4.73% is the base-case risk and the core reason the verdict is RED.

VIX still above 25 — the VIX dropped 24.63% to 27.05 Monday but has popped back toward 28–30 pre-open. A fear gauge this high fattens the overnight gap tail in both directions — any reversal of the melt-up gaps hard.

December 9 Fed hike ~94% priced — the likeliest outcome is a 25bp hike, at 94%, at the December 9, 2026 meeting. A rate backdrop tightening into a still-correcting tape caps any relief rally and pressures high-multiple tech.

Nvidia / AI-trade concentration — Nvidia shares jumped about 31% after the board reinstated Jensen Huang, lifting AI suppliers and helping the Nasdaq rally more than 6%. A single name driving the whole move means a single headline can reverse it — NVDA was already down ~5% pre-open Tuesday.
Thin holiday-week liquidity & data — a holiday-shortened week with PCE/GDP in the flow. Low liquidity plus data into a two-sided tape can amplify any move — the week's biggest tail.
